page: Vultr vcg-l40s-16c-180g-48vram is a Cloud GPU server configured with an Intel Xeon 6448H processor featuring 16 physical cores and 16 vCPUs on an x86_64 architecture. The CPU operates at a base frequency of 2.0 GHz with a shared allocation model and lacks hyperthreading. It is equipped with 180.0 GB of system memory, providing 11.25 GB per core. For acceleration, the server integrates a single NVIDIA L40S GPU based on the Ada Lovelace architecture, delivering 48 GB of dedicated VRAM. Local storage consists of a 1200 GB NVMe SSD.

Benchmark data highlights strong performance in specific data processing and machine learning tasks. The server achieves top-tier results in LLM inference, processing 13631.52 tokens per second for prompts and 610.8 tokens per second for generation on a small 135M model, alongside 6293.73 tokens per second for prompts and 153.1 tokens per second for generation on a medium 7B model. Single-threaded bzip3 decompression reaches top-tier levels at 15.59 GB/sec, while multi-threaded bzip3 decompression is strong at 238.14 GB/sec. Standard CPU and memory benchmarks, such as stress-ng and Passmark, consistently register in the average range, indicating that the system's primary performance advantage lies in its GPU-accelerated capabilities rather than raw general-purpose CPU compute.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the server offers a high density of GPU VRAM and system memory relative to its 16-vCPU count, making it a specialized resource for workloads that require substantial memory capacity without needing massive CPU core counts. This hardware profile is highly suited for large language model inference, deep learning training, data science pipelines, and memory-intensive GPU-accelerated database operations.
description: Vultr vcg-l40s-16c-180g-48vram is a GPU-accelerated cloud server designed for memory-intensive and machine learning workloads. It features an Intel Xeon 6448H processor with 16 physical cores and 16 vCPUs on an x86_64 architecture, running at 2.0 GHz with shared CPU allocation. The system is equipped with 180.0 GB of RAM, a 1200 GB NVMe SSD, and a single NVIDIA L40S GPU with 48 GB of VRAM. Benchmarks demonstrate top-tier performance in LLM inference, achieving 6293.73 tokens per second for prompt processing on a medium 7B model, and strong bzip3 decompression speeds. While general CPU and memory benchmarks perform in the average tier, the server's high VRAM-to-vCPU ratio provides qualitative cost efficiency for specialized tasks. It is highly suited for LLM inference, deep learning, and GPU-accelerated data processing.
